issue_context.title: Multiple LoadBalancer in the same cluster compete with each other
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->

/sig network

**What happened**:
A use case has arisen where multiple LoadBalancers can be present within the same cluster. 

specifically, in the case where a hybrid cluster with both OpenStack workers and Bare-Metal workers.  In this scenario, Octavia is used as the LoadBalancer within K8s with the openstack-controller-manager CNI.  Also, MetalLB is used.  

The Idea is that one could migrate a workload off of OpenStack/Octavia, and into a hybrid world with MetalLB, and thus the workload could float between Openstack and Bare-Metal workers.

When having both LoadBalancer present at the same time, whenever a Service type LoadBalancer is created, BOTH LBs will provide an address.  The first one to respond, in this case always MetalLB, will be what the service grabs and stop looking at the other LB.

**What you expected to happen**:
Expected would be some API mechanism, or Label, or Annotation to allow the choice of which LoadBalancer to use.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Deploy charmed Kubernetes inside of Openstack Train with Octavia enabled and configured.  Deploy Openstack Integrator into the same model and relate it to kubernetes master with loadbalancer relation.  This will automatically install openstack-controller-manager for LoadBalancer requests.

Install MetalLB 0.9.3 via manifest following installation guide on MetalLB site.

Deploy a POD and either expose it as type LoadBalancer or create a service in the manifest.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
It has been tried with setting both openstack specific annotations as well as metallb annotations in the service.  None change the behavior.  

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.17.2
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Openstack Stein with Octavia
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Ubuntu 18.04
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 4.15.0-91-generic
- Install tools: Juju / Charmed Kubernetes
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug): openstack-cloud-controller-manager via openstack-integrator.  MetalLB 0.9.3 installed via manifest
- Others:

Hi @jeff-hillman and thanks for raising this issue.

Inside Kubernetes, the responsible for dealing with the objects reconciliation are the controller manager. Specifically for cloud objects (like Openstack, AWS and so on) there's a special component called cloud-controller-manager for each cloud provider.

What should support in this case this kind of 'object filtering' based in annotation or label is each cloud-controller, in openstack case is https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-openstack. 

As an example, in the past the NGINX Ingress controller used to filter this with a ``ingress-class`` annotation that other ingress controllers (HAProxy as an example) could rely to see which ingress objects they should deal or not, and this became a standard later. But this was much more the ingress controllers internal implementation that something directly related to Kubernetes.

In the case of the LoadBalancer I don't know really if this is something that could be defaulted as a field from Service instead of an annotation or a label, but my point is that IMO this is much more something that each controller should support other than be something, right now related to an API change to support inside a Service object an extra loadbalancer-class field.  Remembering either any way (field in service object or annotation, the controller that creates the LoadBalancer should support this).

My suggestion for you, right now would be to open an issue for the cloud providers to support (Openstack and MetalLB) to support some annotation or label filtering feature for the objects.

Let me know if I can help with anything else.

/cc @andrewsykim Andrew, I'm cc you per @aojea suggestion, as this might be something useful for cloud providers

/kind support
/remove-triage unresolved

You want a service annotation `kubernetes.io/loadbalancer.class`, if absent keep current behavior, if present check if we are the right controller ?

@jeff-hillman great, this makes sense to you?

If so, I think we can close this issue and wait for each controller to support this. I hope Andrew also can take a look into this issue to put some thoughts :)

I'll put some thought into it. I think the class annotation is probably a hard sell for Services, but maybe a "ignore this Service" annotation read by service controller can work to at least disable cloud providers. That in addition to a class annotation read by MetalLB would let you do what you're looking for.
@andrewsykim `kubernetes.io/loadbalancer.class: openstack` means everyone else than openstack please ignore this service, no need for multiple annotations

> @andrewsykim kubernetes.io/loadbalancer.class: openstack means everyone else than openstack please ignore this service, no need for multiple annotations

Right, but that requires everyone else to watch that class annotation and ignore the Service if the "class" doesn't match. Today if your cloud provider is enabled, it owns all Service Type=LoadBalancer. Changing that default behavior may be tricky.

If you want 2 LoadBalancer controller (say MetalLB and OpenStack) to run side by side, today you must modify both, so better have only 1 annotation and modify controller if it make sense.

You don't need to modify GCP/AWS/Azure/... cloud controller because you are not going to run another LoadBalancer controller with them, they can stick to the default behaviour of owning all the `Type=LoadBalancer` services.

> You don't need to modify GCP/AWS/Azure/... cloud controller because you are not going to run another LoadBalancer controller with them

Exactly, I wouldn't be in favor of adding a first class annotation based one provider's use-case. If OpenStack wants to support a custom annotation to ignore a Service Type=LoadBalancer so you can run it along side MetalLB that would be a conversation to have in https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-openstack.  

If there are use-cases to support multiple loadbalancer controllers in other providers (e.g. MetalLB on an AWS/Azure/GCP clusters), I think that would require a large discussion and probably a proposal.

The conversation needs to happen in openstack-cloud-provider and MetalLB and ..., so kubernetes repo/this ticket is kind of the right place to have this conversation IMO.
Also having feedback on the limitations on using a simple annotation and why Ingress switched away from it

IMO there are two paths: 
* The fastest one is to ask for each LB provider to support the annotation ``kubernetes.io/loadbalancer.class: openstack`` UNTIL
* This gets supported by the new Service APIs which I think will deal with loadbalancer class (https://kubernetes-sigs.github.io/service-apis/concepts/#gatewayclass_1)

@rikatz I'm not sure how the latter would help.  I did some reading on the link you proposed, and I don't see how that could select the appropriate LB.

also, please note if it helps, that the use case i'm working on, actually have the same Physical Gateway.  In Openstack I'm using VLAN / Provider networking, so both OS LB and MetalLB use the same gateway address.

My point in the second link was, as the service api is being redesigned, there's a Gateway Class (in the meaning of the gateway to inside the network, not out) that can be used to select which resource will deal with the ingress traffic (the load balancer).

Here: https://kubernetes-sigs.github.io/service-apis/concepts/#gatewayclass

As far as I remember from this API spec, the cluster admin will define a GatewayClass and when you ask for a Gateway from a specific GatewayClass it will be created in the LB provider selected by this GatewayClass.

To be fair, I don't know / can't remember if the covered case here is like "a cloud load balancer with different tier / kind of service' or this might also be helpful in cases such as 'I've a cluster, I want that the 'production' services with a 'production' GatewayClass gets a Cloud Provider Load Balancer, while the 'non-production' gets my own MetalLB and I wont spend in a Cloud Provided expensive Load Balancer"

I don't think we want to add ServiceClass or service.class.  Gateway is the approach for that.

I wouldn't necessarily shoot-down a single label which deactivated the cloud-controller's service controller, so you could do whatever you want external to that.  That said, it sounds like you really want a "custom" cloud provider module that implements this hybrid world exactly how you want it. 

If you want to pursue what @andrewsykim suggested, your EASIEST path is to do it entirely within the OpenStack provider.  The more painful approach would be to do it in generic service controller.

What do you want to do?  I don't think this is a si-gnet issue any more, BTW :)
